coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 13
record.summary: Planned mixed-use block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan, in the 4.8-acre area at 22nd and Illinois Streets that PG&E owns and operates as an electrical switchyard; the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 gives it 85 ft and 125 ft height limits, and its build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and is not vacant land: per SF Planning's project page and the final D4D (Figure 1.2.1, printed p.12) it lies in the 4.8-acre area at 22nd and Illinois Streets that PG&E owns and operates as an electrical switchyard (the D4D's 'PG&E Sub-area'), whose build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation. DataSF Parcels lists an active lot with an address, 4175499 (1101 Illinois St, recorded 2024-10-15), covering nearly all of this approximate footprint; the dataset does not say whether that lot is the switchyard parcel. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, positioned by matching several points on it to real streets, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 with a refined multi-point georeferencing of the diagram, re-measured the same day consistently across the whole block layout, and re-corrected the same day after a mis-measured reference point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Block 13's land is not part of the developer-owned 21-acre Power Station parcel: it is in the 4.8-acre PG&E-owned northern switchyard (final D4D Figure 1.2.1; SF Planning project page), which the Master Plan includes but whose build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation and on the property coming within the Development Agreement's jurisdiction. DataSF Parcels lists an active lot, 4175499 (1101 Illinois St, recorded 2024-10-15), overlapping about 99% of this approximate footprint; whether it is PG&E's switchyard parcel is not established, so this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) shows Block 13 permits Residential, Institutional, Retail, Non-Retail Sales/Services (office), Entertainment and PDR uses (PDR limited to listed uses at the lower floors); Laboratory and Life Science are not permitted. Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D gives Block 13 two height limits by its colour-coded labels, 85 ft and 125 ft; the '300'MAX' and '280'MAX' labels on the block sit on tick-ended dimension lines (plan extents of the 125 ft zone), not heights, and Standard 6.2.2 lists Block 13 among the midrise buildings (101-145 ft). The tallest limit on the site is Block 7's 240 ft. No construction-start source found.

changes.text: Block 13's record and map notes no longer say the D4D shows 280 ft and 300 ft towers: on Figure 6.2.3 those labels are dimension lines, and the block's height limits are 85 ft and 125 ft, so the alleged inconsistency with the midrise text is removed. The block is now described as sitting in the 4.8-acre PG&E-owned northern switchyard area (SF Planning project page; D4D Figure 1.2.1), not vacant land, with build-out dependent on the switchyard's relocation; an addressed Assessor lot (4175499, 1101 Illinois St) overlaps the footprint but is not confirmed as that parcel. The 2035 completion is kept as a Phase 3 forecast from SocketSite's October 2020 schedule table (Block 13 vertical development 2031-2035) instead of a whole-project target. Sources now point to the final D4D rather than a dead 2019 draft link, D4D publishers are shown as SF Planning, and one image is labelled a document, not a rendering.

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 13; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.

Corrected 2026-09-29: an earlier version of this dossier read the '300'MAX' and '280'MAX' labels on Figure 6.2.3 as heights and reported a conflict with Standard 6.2.2; they are dimension lines (plan extents), and the block's heights are 85 ft and 125 ft, within the midrise range. The D4D's Appendix A.12 is titled 'Block 13 Controls (Low-rise Building)' while Standard 6.2.2 lists Block 13 as midrise (101-145 ft); the difference in labels is unexplained.
Block 13's 2031-2035 window comes from a 2020 press table (SocketSite) and is contingent on the PG&E switchyard's relocation; no current Block 13 schedule was found.

DataSF Parcels lists an active addressed lot (4175499, 1101 Illinois St) over this block's approximate footprint; whether it is PG&E's switchyard parcel is not established, and whether this record's map shape should follow it has not been decided.

record.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted block (final D4D, Feb 26, 2020: Table 3.1.1 and Figure 6.2.3) -- see the accuracy caveat. Status 'planned' is contingent: the D4D's Appendix E says portions of the PG&E Sub-area 'may or may not ultimately be redeveloped', and the SF Planning project page says build-out of the PG&E lands depends on relocating the switchyard; SocketSite (Oct 2020) lists Block 13 in Phase 3. Use 'mixed': residential, retail, office and PDR uses are permitted (D4D Table 3.1.1).
